findings.message: uses eval() or new Function() to execute dynamically generated code
findings.remediation: Remove dynamic evaluation and use fixed allowlisted implementations.
findings.impact: Dynamic eval/Function executes code that is difficult to audit and becomes code injection if external input reaches it.
findings.attack_vector: Source uses eval()/new Function(); this rule alone does not prove that an attacker controls the evaluated value.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: dynamically imports code from a variable path
findings.remediation: Use static imports with allowlisted modules; avoid dynamic import() with variable arguments.
findings.impact: Dynamic import() with variable paths allows loading arbitrary modules at runtime.
findings.attack_vector: import(variablePath) — attacker controls the path to inject malicious modules.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: accesses system or user credential stores
findings.remediation: Avoid direct access to credential files; use authenticated API flows instead.
findings.impact: Direct access to system credential stores allows theft of SSH keys, AWS creds, and Docker tokens.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Use a safe, schema-validating format and never deserialize attacker-controlled bytes with executable loaders.
findings.impact: Unsafe deserialization can instantiate attacker-controlled objects and trigger arbitrary code execution.
findings.attack_vector: pickle, dill, marshal, node-serialize, or unsafe YAML loaders consume untrusted bytes.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
